BulkEntryIn.description:
One name to add, either as text or as an existing student the teacher picked.

Exactly one of the two. `student_id` is how the preview's `enrol_existing` and
`ambiguous` verdicts get committed — it is the teacher saying "this child", which no
amount of name matching can establish on its own.
BulkEntryIn.title: BulkEntryIn

ChildDocumentPatch.description: Rename and/or move a child's file. Never its content — see the module docstring.
ChildDocumentPatch.title: ChildDocumentPatch

ChosenValue.description: A value the child chooses in their own program (`ships`), and what it must be.
ChosenValue.title: ChosenValue

ClassCurriculumIn.description:
The course a class follows and the lesson it is on. Both fields are always sent.

A PUT rather than a PATCH field on the class: the two values constrain each other (the
lesson must be in the course), so they are set together and validated together.
ClassCurriculumIn.title: ClassCurriculumIn

ClassDetailOut.description:
A class plus its join code.

Separate from `ClassOut` so the list route does not have to fetch a code per class.
A teacher reads the code off the class itself, not off a list of twelve of them.
Mirrors the StudentOut / StudentDetailOut split in the roster router.
ClassDetailOut.title: ClassDetailOut

ClassPatch.description: Every field optional — an absent field means "leave it alone".
ClassPatch.title: ClassPatch

CompareTest.description:
"Matches my solution" (Ken's decision, 17 Oct 2026): the child's program and the
reference solution are run on every case, with the child's `chosen` values put into
the solution, and their output compared. Correct checks for student-chosen data, with
no code to write. See `runtime/grader.py`.

`reference` is the scrambled solution, added only when the check is sent to a child's
browser (`with_reference`) — never stored, and null in a teacher's document.
CompareTest.title: CompareTest

DocumentPatch.description: Every field optional — an absent field means "leave it alone".
DocumentPatch.title: DocumentPatch

DocumentSummaryOut.description:
A row in the file list. Deliberately without `content`.

The list is fetched whenever the editor loads, and a child with a term of work in six
files should not be downloading all of it to render a sidebar.
DocumentSummaryOut.title: DocumentSummaryOut

EraseIn.description: Delete entirely: the name, typed out, as the confirmation (case and spaces ignored).
EraseIn.title: EraseIn

ExampleDoc.description:
A sample run a child can watch. `inputs` are typed in order, one per `input()`.

`transcript` is what the reference solution's run looked like, filled at publish; on a
draft it is always None.
ExampleDoc.title: ExampleDoc

FileLinkIn.description: The child's file to keep this work in, or null to stop.
FileLinkIn.title: FileLinkIn

FolderPatch.description: Rename and/or move. An absent field is left alone; `parent_id: null` is the top.
FolderPatch.title: FolderPatch

FunctionTest.description:
Run the program, then evaluate `call` and compare it with `expected` using `==`.

Both are Python expressions: `call="add(2, 3)"`, `expected="5"`.
FunctionTest.title: FunctionTest

HintDoc.description: One rung. Unlocks when either threshold is met; zero for both means "always open".
HintDoc.title: HintDoc

HomeworkPatch.description: Every field optional — an absent field means "leave it alone".
HomeworkPatch.title: HomeworkPatch

IoTest.description:
Feed `stdin` to the program, compare what it prints with `expected`.

`exact` ignores trailing whitespace on each line and trailing blank lines — a child
failing a test over a stray space learns nothing about Python. `contains` passes when
`expected` appears anywhere in the output.
IoTest.title: IoTest

reset_existing.description: False issues a PIN only to students who have none. True regenerates for everyone on the roster, which is the answer to 'the slips got lost'.
reset_existing.title: Reset Existing

NextHintOut.description: The next rung, without its text. `available` is the server's verdict right now.
NextHintOut.title: NextHintOut

NodePatch.description: Every field optional — an absent field means "leave it alone".
NodePatch.title: NodePatch

OptionCountOut.description: One answer to a multiple-choice question, and how many children chose it.
OptionCountOut.title: OptionCountOut

OptionDoc.description:
One answer to a multiple-choice question.

A wrong option should name the wrong belief that leads to it — "thinks range includes
the end" — so a teacher can read the class's answers as a list of misconceptions
(spec §3.6). Optional, because a teacher may not always know; publishing warns.
OptionDoc.title: OptionDoc

PinIn.description: A PIN the teacher chose, or none for a random one.
PinIn.title: PinIn

PinSlipOut.description:
A PIN in plaintext: on setting it, to print and hand over, or from Show PIN.

Stored as an Argon2id hash plus an encrypted copy (app/auth/pin.py). Every response
carrying one is a POST marked no-store, so it never sits in a URL or an HTTP cache.
PinSlipOut.title: PinSlipOut

ProblemSummaryOut.description: A row in the bank list — no code, no tests, no hints.
ProblemSummaryOut.title: ProblemSummaryOut

PublishIn.description:
Proof the teacher's browser ran the solution against the tests of *this* version.

`verified_updated_at` is the `updated_at` the editor had when its run passed. A save
in another tab since then moves `updated_at`, and the publish is refused — the run
proved something about a version that no longer exists.
PublishIn.title: PublishIn

RandomInput.description: `count` whole numbers picked from `start`..`end` — the same ones on every press.
RandomInput.title: RandomInput

RangeInput.title: RangeInput

RosterEntryOut.description: A student as seen from inside a class: who they are, plus how they got there.
RosterEntryOut.title: RosterEntryOut

truncated.title: Truncated

RunIn.description: One press of Run (no result) or Check (with a result).
RunIn.title: RunIn

ScriptTest.description:
The teacher's own Python check (17 Oct 2026), for what a fixed expected value cannot
say — a check that depends on values the child chose.

`code` gets `run(*inputs)`, which runs the child's program and returns `(output,
variables)`, and `check(condition, message)`. See `runtime/grader.py`.
ScriptTest.title: ScriptTest

StartedProblemOut.description: A lesson problem the child has opened, for My work's Lessons tab.
StartedProblemOut.title: StartedProblemOut

StudentClassOut.description: One class a student has been in, from the student's side.
StudentClassOut.title: StudentClassOut

StudentCreatedOut.description: A new account, with its PIN — to print or tell the child.
StudentCreatedOut.title: StudentCreatedOut

StudentIn.description:
A new account (Ken's decision, 11 Oct 2026): a name, a username and a PIN.

Leave `username` out and one is suggested from the name; leave `pin` out and a random
one is drawn. Either way the PIN comes back in the response, to print or tell; after
that, Show PIN reveals it again (16 Oct 2026).
StudentIn.title: StudentIn

StudentPatch.title: StudentPatch

post.description: Stop further hand-ins. Children can still see the sheet and their feedback.

get.description: The sheet's questions with how many are handed in and marked, and the class.
One question, every child's answer to it, in roster order.

post.description:
Mark every answered, unmarked multiple-choice answer to one question: Correct 2 for
the right option, 0 for any other. A teacher can still change any of them, or add a
comment, afterwards. Code questions are never marked automatically — approach is a
human call.

put.description: The optional overall note to one child on this homework.

post.description:
Give marked work back. Every mark and note not yet released goes out together.

Children with no mark are untouched — they can still hand in, and are released next
time. A child who has something back finds their sheet read-only.
Give the draft to the class. It appears for them at once.

put.description:
Mark one child's answer to one question. Marks the latest hand-in; marking a child
who never handed in takes a copy of their saved work first, so the mark always points
at the exact code it judged.

get.description:
Who am I? The web app calls this on load to decide whether to bootstrap.

The dependency has already verified the token and resolved the principal, so this
reads by id rather than verifying a second time.

Whether this address has been invited. A yes or a no, and nothing else.

No sign-in needed: the person asking does not have an account yet. It says nothing
about who invited them, when, or whether they already have an account.

post.description: End this session. Idempotent — signing out twice is not an error.

get.description: Who am I? The web app calls this on load to decide which screen to show.

post.description: Username plus PIN, in exchange for a session cookie.

Exchange a verified Supabase token for a profile, provisioning on first use.

Idempotent: called twice, the second call returns the same profile rather than
creating a second row.

Create a class, with the join code it will keep for its whole life.

The code is minted here rather than by a separate 'generate a code' action,
because a class that exists but cannot be joined is not a state worth being able
to reach. It is an attribute of the class, like its name.

Close a class: hide it from the default list, revoke its join codes, sign its
children out. This is the class page's "Remove class".

Enrolments are left untouched. They are the record of who was actually in the class
this term, which is exactly what Phase 8 mastery reads — withdrawing them on archive
would overwrite history to tidy up a status field.

Children still signed in are signed out, as when one child is removed from a class: a
session belongs to the child, so without this they would carry on working in a class
that no longer exists for anyone else. They can sign in to any other class they are in.

put.description:
Choose the class's course and today's lesson.

The lesson must sit in the chosen course, and both must be active — a class pointed at
an archived lesson would show children a ladder the teacher can no longer see to edit.
A lesson with no course is refused rather than inferred: guessing the course from the
lesson would silently change what the class follows.

Ids from another centre come back 404 through scoping, as everywhere, rather than as
a 422 that would confirm they exist.

post.description:
Delete a class entirely: it and its homework, quizzes, submissions and marks (Ken's
decision, 11 Oct 2026). Student accounts and their own files stay — a child can be in
other classes. Owner only, with the class name typed out. See `app.erase`.

Enrol an existing centre student into a class.

Both ids are resolved through `scoping`, so a class in another centre and a student in
another centre are each a 404 — and so is the cross pairing, which is the case worth
having a test for.
Undo a withdrawal, reusing the original enrolment row.

Take a student out of a class. The enrolment row stays; its status changes.

The child is signed out too. A session belongs to the student, not to a class, so
without this a child removed mid-lesson would carry on working in the class they were
just taken out of until the session expired. They can sign in again only to a class
they are still in — the join flow needs an active enrolment.

get.description: The class's homework, newest first. Archived ones are left out.

schema.title: Response List Homework Classes  Class Id  Homework Get

post.description: Start a homework as a draft. Nothing is visible to the class until it is set.

Replace the class's join code, invalidating the old one immediately.

The remedy for a code that has got out — read out to the wrong room, photographed off
a whiteboard. There is no standalone revoke to pair with this: rotating leaves the
class joinable, whereas revoking alone would leave a class with children on its roster
and no way in, which is not a state worth being one click away.

Issue PINs across a class and return the slips.

The bulk counterpart to bulk roster entry: having pasted twelve names, a teacher is
not going to set twelve PINs one form at a time. By default this only touches
children who have no PIN yet, so it is safe to run again after adding one student.

get.description: The class roster, alphabetically — the order it is read aloud in.

schema.title: Response Read Roster Classes  Class Id  Roster Get

post.description:
Commit a reviewed paste: create the new children, enrol all of them, in one go.

All-or-nothing. Anything unresolved — a blank or over-long name, a name the centre has
twice, the same name twice in one submission, a name that would collide with a
classmate — rejects the whole request with 422 and writes nothing. A teacher fixing
one line should not have to work out which of the other eleven already went through.

Names are re-resolved here rather than taken on trust from the preview: a client that
posts `{"display_name": "Bella N"}` for a Bella N the centre already knows gets her
enrolled, not duplicated. The preview is an affordance for the teacher; this is the
authority. An entry that names a `student_id` is the teacher having chosen a specific
child, and skips matching entirely.

Entries that are already enrolled are accepted and skipped, so re-submitting a paste
verbatim is safe rather than an error.

schema.title: Response Bulk Enrol Classes  Class Id  Roster Bulk Post

post.description:
Read a pasted list of names and say what committing it would do.

Writes nothing — no students, no enrolments, no audit row. A teacher reads this back
before anything happens to a child's record, which is the point of splitting the paste
into two requests at all.

Create a child's account and put them in this class — the class page's Add student.

Returns the slip (name, username, PIN) to print; Show PIN reveals it again later.

Undo an archive.

Revoked join codes stay revoked — reviving a code nobody expects to work again is a
worse surprise than issuing a fresh one.

Plan, and optionally apply, a YAML file of problems (see `app/problem_import.py`).

A file with any bad entry applies nothing, and says which entries to fix. Always a 200:
a file with mistakes in it is the normal first draft of a file, not a failed request.

put.description: Replace a draft with the document sent. Anything else is a 409.

post.description: Take a problem out of the bank. Sets that already use it keep it.

A draft copy of a published problem, to edit and publish in its place.

If a draft of the next version already exists it is returned rather than a second one
made: two teachers pressing "edit" on the same problem should land on the same draft.
Make a draft available to sets — and retire the version it replaces, if any.

Bring a problem back as a draft.

Always to draft, never straight to published: a newer version may have been published
while this one was put away, and a re-publish runs the tests again anyway.

put.description:
Replace the concepts a lesson introduces.

Every id must be a concept this centre can see — a global one, or the centre's own.
Accepting any concept id would let a centre tag with another centre's private
concept, which is a cross-tenant reference even if nothing reads through it yet. An
unknown id is a 422 naming nothing, the same as a missing one would be.

A problem as the child sees it, with their attempt at each part.

A POST because the first open creates the attempts — which is also what starts the
clock the hint ladder's minutes are measured from.

patch.description: Autosave. Like a file save, a save that changes nothing writes nothing.

put.description: Pick an answer to a multiple-choice question. Changeable until handed in or time is up.

Save this work to one of the child's own files, from now on (the Save window).

The file is written straight away with the work as it is. Only a live file of their own
can be chosen — another child's is a 404, as everywhere.

post.description: Unlock the next rung, if the child has earned it. Rungs open in order.

Count a Run or a Check. A Check also records how many tests passed.

The result is the browser's word, and is used for the teacher's progress view, never
for marks: homework is re-run in the teacher's browser at marking time (Phase 5).

get.description: The saved layout, or `saved: false` for a teacher who has never arranged one.

schema.title: Response List Documents Me Documents Get

post.description:
Start a new file.

Both fields are optional, because the common case is a child pressing "new file" with
nothing in mind. An untitled file gets a number rather than a collision: the partial
unique index would refuse a second "untitled.py", and a 409 in response to pressing a
plus button is not an error a ten-year-old can act on.

patch.description:
Save. This is the autosave endpoint, so it is the busiest route in the product.

A save that changes nothing writes nothing — `TimestampMixin` has `onupdate`, so
touching the row would move `updated_at` and reshuffle the file list under a child who
is only reading. The same reasoning as the no-op PATCH on classes and students.

post.description:
Delete a file: it goes to the child's Trash ("Recently deleted") for 30 days.

Never straight to gone (Ken, 23 Oct 2026): a child who tidies up mid-term must not be
able to destroy a term of their own work with one tap, and a child cannot empty their
Trash themselves (`app/trash.py`).

Bring a file back out of the Trash (`app/trash.py`), to its folder if that is still
there and to the top level if not. A name taken meanwhile is a 409, as for a rename.

Everything the home screen shows: today's ladder, and homework — due, handed in,
or given back. Soonest due first; returned work after everything still to do.

Every lesson problem the child has started, last worked on first (17 Oct 2026).

So a child can carry on at home with a problem from an earlier lesson: Today only shows
the class's current one. Classwork only — homework and quizzes have their own tabs.
Reached through the child's active enrolments and open assignments, as everything is.

Delete a snippet for good (Ken, 23 Oct 2026). No Trash: it is one line of a
teacher's own wording with nothing attached — a comment already given keeps its text,

Create a child's account at the centre, without enrolling them anywhere.

get.description: What the Add student form fills in as the teacher types the name.

patch.description: Rename a student — most often to add a last initial after a name clash.

post.description:
The child has left the academy: withdraw them from their classes and sign them out.

This is the one place the roster diverges from `archive_class`, which deliberately
leaves enrolments alone. The asymmetry is real rather than an oversight. Archiving a
*class* means the term ended and nobody left, so withdrawing its enrolments would
overwrite history to tidy a status field. Archiving a *student* means the child left,
and withdrawal is the honest record of that — the rows keep their `joined_at`, so a
term of history survives intact.

Live sessions are revoked in the same breath, because an archived student must not
still be signed in on a centre laptop.

Delete a child entirely: their account and all their work, everywhere (Ken's
decision, 11 Oct 2026). Owner only, and only with the name typed out. See `app.erase`.

post.description:
Change a child's PIN — to one the teacher chose, or a random one.

The remedy for a PIN that was set before Show PIN existed, or that a classmate has
seen. The slip comes back to print.

Show PIN: a child's current PIN, for a teacher without the slip (16 Oct 2026).

Any teacher at the centre may look — every teacher can open every class — and each look
is a `pin.viewed` row, so "who has seen this child's PIN" is answerable. A POST, not a
GET, so the PIN never lands in a URL, browser history or an HTTP cache.

Kick a student's session — wrong child signed in, or a laptop left open.

Takes effect on the next request rather than at expiry, which is the whole reason the
session token is opaque and revocable rather than a JWT.

Undo an archive.

Withdrawn enrolments stay withdrawn, mirroring `unarchive_class` leaving revoked join
codes revoked. A child coming back does not necessarily rejoin the same class, and
silently re-enrolling them into last term's is a worse surprise than enrolling them
explicitly.
